per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at the N terminus and two surface loops, on an otherwise rigid domain. RelaxDB source paper now read in full (apo, 25 °C, pH 6.0, 50 mM MES, 1.0 mM, 600 MHz): S2 above 0.8 for most of the 63 fitted residues with an internal correlation time of about 70 ps, lower S2 at the N terminus and in the loops between strands 3 and 4 and between 4 and 5; an axially anisotropic diffusion tensor was preferred over the isotropic tau_c of 6.28 ns (SILB-J1). Per-residue values exist only in Figure S6.
per_window.us-ms: unresolved by the single-field Rex rule: in the apo reference state exchange terms are confined to the metal-binding loop, at Ala24, Gln29, Gly31, Ala32, Met33 and Met35 (fitted Rex), with raised R2 also at His22, highest at Gln29 (about 6 s-1) and Met35 (about 4.3 s-1), with apo R2 raised to 11-15 s-1 against a baseline near 8 s-1 (SILB-J2); no exchange term is fitted outside that loop (SILB-J9, measured_not_detected). One equivalent of Ag+ removes the excess relaxation (SILB-J4, measured_not_detected in the bound state). No rate, population or Delta-omega anywhere.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved (search_insufficient): the full text contains no hydrogen-exchange, time-resolved, FRET or EPR measurement, and the searches for such work returned zero hits (SILB-J3).
per_window.undetermined: In the Ag+-bound sample the Met65 methyl correlation disappears, which the authors presume to be severe line broadening without identifying the process (SILB-J7). The apo structure superposes on apo E. coli CusF with a backbone rmsd of 1.17 A, a homolog similarity, not a second state (SILB-J8). The 2016 paper studies a different construct, the N-terminal plus membrane-proximal domains (SILB-J5), and its finding that the C-terminal site fills first is binding, not motion (SILB-J6).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, in one loop and without a rate: the free wild-type SilB C-terminal domain at 25 °C, pH 6.0 in 50 mM MES (600 MHz, single field, R1rho-derived R2) carries exchange terms of about 1.5-6 s-1 confined to the metal-binding loop, at Ala24, Gln29, Gly31, Ala32, Met33 and Met35 (fitted Rex), with raised R2 also at His22, highest at Gln29 at the top of the loop and at the Cu+ ligand Met35; the rest of the domain is rigid with S2 above 0.8. No exchange rate, population or chemical-shift difference was measured, one equivalent of Ag+ abolishes the excess relaxation, and the authors state that the apo protein does not simply exchange with a conformation close to the metal-bound one.
questions_for_gina: Is the RelaxDB 17266 set the 2011 apo sample (25 °C, pH 6.0, 50 mM MES, 600 MHz), or does it also include the Ag+-bound relaxation data of the same paper?
The paper prints 'Ala31' while the sequence has Gly31 and Ala32, and Figure S6C shows exchange at both positions: should the atlas keep both residues, as here, or ask the authors?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi200005k) was read in full on 2026-10-20 (case S6_r6_17266_20261020221901), superseding the abstract-only row SILB-r1, which is no longer cited; the 2016 paper on the other construct (doi:10.1021/acs.biochem.6b00022) is still an abstract. All samples are 1.0 mM protein in 50 mM MES at pH 6.0 and 25 °C; apo, Ag+ (1 equivalent) and Cu+ (with 10 equivalents of ascorbate) are separate sample states and are not combined. R2 comes from an R1rho decay, not from a CPMG series, and the model-free fit was made on the apo sample only; per-residue S2, tau_i and Rex exist only as Figure S6, so the values quoted here are read from that plot. Thr34 was not fitted and overlapping resonances were excluded, leaving 63 apo and 57 Ag+-bound residues. Both readers passed all four rows of this case with no flags. The results text prints 'axially isotropic' where the methods and Figure S6 say axially anisotropic (SILB-J1).

judgments.reason: Full text: adding one equivalent of Ag+ removes the excess transverse relaxation of the metal-binding loop while overall tumbling and fast backbone mobility stay similar, which the authors state as slow motions in the apo state that are abolished once the metal is bound; this is absence of detectable exchange in the bound state at this field, not proof that the loop has stopped moving (sources_cache/10.1021_bi200005k.pdf, pp. 2196, 2199-2200, Figure 6A-B).
